$comment: Which mascot pose fills which landing-page slot, and where each one came from — plus the
library of supplied poses that fill no slot yet. Every PNG in public/mascot/poses/ is a
`supplied` entry: hand-cut art the project owner pasted in, or a trimmed, downscaled copy
of the owner's action art in public/mascot/actions/. Every file on disk has a record here,
so an asset's provenance is always the `origin` its entry gives (spec 5.2: a slot may only
be filled from a source whose origin is recorded).
History: until 2026-10-08 a `poses` array held five assets that scripts/mascot/extract.js
cut from two character sheets (greeting, noting, holding-memory, looking-ahead, resting).
The owner ruled those cuts broken (soft fringe, low resolution); they were deleted with
extract.js and replaced by crisper action art (see each landing slot's `origin`).
`width`/`height` are the exported pixel size — roughly 3x the largest size the slot
renders at, so the asset holds up on a high-DPI screen without shipping the 1300px source.
A `supplied` entry carries a `slot` only while it fills a landing-page slot

supplied.slot: §8 CTA, at the right-hand end of the centred band. The only unused supplied pose that is SITTING ON an orb, which is what cta.mascotAlt — the owner's copy, and the binding description of what ships — says the image shows. reading-on-the-orb.png is the other and §6 has it; lying-prone.png is lying, not sitting, and would make the alt text false for anyone who cannot see the image. Differs from 346:6275 (eyes open, ring-less orb): the reference is a flattened PNG and the hand-cut library wins, the same reasoning the owner used to close §6's icon question.
